THIS IS A LONG AND FULL REVIEW OF GAMEPLAY, prepare to do a lot of reading (but is worth the read for a good critque, in my opinion).
(For some reason Steam thinks the word C-L-I-T-C-H-E is the word that rhymes with "rich" and describes a woman you hate, so if you see a sensored word in the area titled story, that's why)
For the record even with the new patches that have come out I still have crashes on my PC:
i7-4810MQ Quad 2.8 GHz, 840GT NVIDEA Card, 8GB RAM, up-to-date graphics software, Win 7. etc...
BUT I found a solution, If I cahnge my Laptop's resolution (I use a gaming laptop, I'll get hate for that) to 1360x780 I get ZERO crashing and with patches glitches happen 98% percent less. I can change my Latop's resolution and after that I set the game's resolution Lower. That way it is still Fullscreen BUT my computer can handle it MUCH much much better. So for anyone who can't play much because of crashes, that is one option. Graphics are amazing so it will still look fantastic.
ANYWAY, game critque
PAY TO PLAY:
This game does have some online payment feature that can get you upgrades instead of having to play the story all the way through to get them. Where some people raise ALL KINDS of h-e-l-l for this I clap my hands to Ubisoft. They have a perfect balance of the Pay to Play features; you can beat the game without buying anything (with real money) like I did.
I played out the entire story, it was tough and missions needed TONS of thought put into them but to me that added a sense of difficulty and a challenge that I like.
COMBAT:
This game's combat forces you to have some real skill and also makes you have to refocus how you play the game. I, personally, have always wanted to be more of a stealthy Assassin and avoid direct combat (makes the game more strategic and in my opinion more engaging). Unfortunately, in previous games I was being stealthy for no real reason except to get MAXED OUT syncronization.
In Unity my strategy is almost a necessity because of how tough it is to fight your way through enemies. Enemies have skill and are more broad in terms of categories while also being slightly harder to differentiate making them harder to discriminate in combat on how you fight them. Unity got rid of instant kill counters making the game more realistic in the sense that combat isn't that simple. If you get two experienced fighters or two non-experienced fighters and make them go all out none of them (when fighting their equal) will be able to use magic counters to defeat one-another.
You can still use counters and moves to knock down oppenents to execute them BUT that requires some "grinding" (kinda) in order to learn those skills which, as a player, makes you feel like you're actually gaining knowledge as you continue through the game ( at least I felt that way).
STRATEGY:
This game is the only AC game that actually makes you have to THINK about what you have to do to kill your target. Depending on your style of playing you have ways to tank through soldiers, avoid soldiers and go straight to your target, distract soldiers (and maybe your target) using allies or side-quest aid, etc.
There isn't one way to get your target anymore and with buildings being areas you can freely go in and out of there is more pressure to avoid detection. The reason is that enemies from outside buildings can actually run in after you so there isn't a magic barrier anymore from the outside and the inside.
There are multiple ways to stealtfully attack your target and escape from your target. There isn't one door to a building (at least not always) there are underground routes, direct routes (the front door), side routes (windows and stuff). You have variety which can be essential to how you play.
STEALTH:
Haystacks aren't everywhere....which is normal in actual cities even in older cities of past eras. Without abundunt haystacks you can't just spam hiding corpses (which plays into combat somewhat) so if you kill someone (even with a silent assassination) you run the risk of them, the corpses, being found and you being discovered. If you are discovered you can't just hide anywhere you like so you are more pressured to avoid detection at all costs meaning that you can't just kill every guard you see anymore, making the game much more difficult.
The crouch system is finally here but has flaws. It doesn't let you hide anywhere, just at certain covers areas, sometimes, I have not always been able to take cover when I want, sadly, so it needs to be fixed up a bit.
There isn't a spammed amount of cover anywhere and enemies can also look up if you climb a wall, so not being detected is something you should always aim for.
You also have dozens of ways to escape enemies with smoke and stun grenades. You also have fire crackers to distract guards and make them focuss their attention somewhere other than you so you can sneak past them.
ENEMIES:
Enemies are serious. They are hard to beat, even the lower levels, and I actually found heavy weapon fighter enemies are easier because they are slower. Fast hitting enemies are a pain and have the ability to parry and counter you making you to have to be patient when fighting them, which is hard if you have two other fast hitting enemies and a heavy enemy attacking you at once.
This makes combat nothing to laugh at and you are highly recommended to either bulk up your abilities at hand-to-hand combat and get thicker skin (haha...reference to game's ability) and get better armor (they look like normal clothes in the Customize menu but they're armor) OR you just avoid combat all together and be better at not being detected all the time.
STORY:
Kind of clitche, but so is every popular story eventually. There aren't that many popular themes to choose from. I mean if you watch one movie considered to be a SUSPENSE thiller you've seen about 90% of what is out there in the market. There aren't many unique stories that people can actually stay and listen to on massive scales so I won't criticize the revenage clitche and the romance clitches. Although, I appreciate Arno being a French version of Ezio, he is a good character.
The story builds-up but with its typical theme I could predict Arno's story pretty easily in terms of who is the Templar Grandmaster and blah blah blah...NO spoilers here. The characters are pretty good at connecting with the audience, somewhat, but some do have some transparency but ONE character actually made a good effort to flip the script, BUT I did catch on enough to see it coming (if you played the whole game you may know what I mean, if you haven't play yet well you'll see the surprise soon enough).
But the characters for some reason stop building themselves up. I mean at a certain point (maybe half way) they stop character development and it just focuses on the missions. I actually forgot the purpose of why I was hunting the Templar Grandmaster until they happened to bring it up near the end. So the story has become MUCH more dull but it is still something that some people may like.
I mean in the beginning he makes it clear why he wants to be an Assassin. Then almost until the end you can actually totally forget why he even exists. It kinda sucks....
Also, why does every character (except some NPC's) have a British dialect??? I mean...that was just a ♥♥♥♥ up on Ubisoft's part. Should have found other voice actors for the English translation
Overall I give this game a good 8/10 (though glitches need to be fixed for gameplay to not screw up)

I've seen my share of zombie movies and played my share of zombie games without ever becoming particularly impressed by any. Honestly I find most of them outright stupid, and with the zombie hype that has been going on the last few years the genre as a whole mostly leaves a foul taste in my mouth. But somehow I got talked into watching this show called "The Walking Dead" and it totally blew me over. Well written, great character building and feelings flying all over the board. I found it amazing that something related to zombies could be THAT good.
Then I learned about that this series, or rather the universe of that series, was going to be carried over to an episodic adventure type game by no other than Telltale Games. A company that has helped keeping the adventure genre of gaming alive when it felt almost extinct. As a BIG adventure game fan I have happily supported this company by getting mostly everything they have put out, and that was also mainly the reason I got this series as well.
I honestly had very little expectation of how this game series would be as I failed to see how it even would work to transfer the great writing and suspense that I experienced in the TV-series to an adventure type game. Even though I read good reviews of it I kept putting off playing it. I was absolutely certain that it was going to leave me disappointed.
Well, finally I got around to play it, and now I kick myself fo not playing it sooner. I can not believe how good this game is. I don't think I can remember better storywriting in any game I've played before. You really get to know the characters you meet and you get feelings and opinions about them. You're forced to make tough decisions in critical moments and you can never be sure if you did the right thing. Well, there is not really any clear right or wrong. There is mostly various shades of grey. Not only that, but your decisions affect the ones around you, and they will remember what you did or didn't do, and the game itself shapes itself around all this and creates different routes and takes on what you experience while playing through it.
All characters are masterfully voiced by a selection of excellent voice actors that helps making the experience close to magical. You'll find yourself laughing, crying, yelling at the screen and acting in panic. And you'll probably feel that you're in the middle of it all.
Now, it has to be said that this game is probably not for everybody. I can see, and even understand that people might find the gameplay itself to be a bit dull or repetetive and probably feel there is little gameplay at all. If you hate QTE's then you might want to shy away if you do not appreciate a good story. Also, even though I quite like the artstyle I see some people being thrown off a bit by the comic like cel shading, and I believe the game would be even better with a bit more realistic touch. It certainly looks good enough in its own way and should in any way be avoided with that as a reason.
I consider this game to be one of those games you absolutely should not allow yourself to miss out on. It is a game for the history books and you would want to tell your grandchildren that you were there to play it.
I rate this game 10/10
Recommended for everybody who appreciate video games, and their mothers too.

Like other gamers, I am sometimes hesitant in seeing a remake of a wonderful classic especially one that stuck to me as a child. Ever since I played this game on a NES system a few decades ago, I recall all the frustration I had when going through some tedious puzzles, yet the joy when solving a problem made it more the worthwhile.
Those who have played the game will likely recall a skull ornament door at the very start of the game. Once inside, the warlock lord makes his first appearance (his eyes anyway) dismissing your quest to stop him and confidently remarks about your imminent death. Alas your journey and the puzzles start immediately. At times you attempt to methodically evaluate and make sense of a problem ahead. In other times, you may resort to trying random actions. Actions which may cause you to progress, cause your death – or even witty remarks to things you wouldn’t do in real life!
Its 2014, a remake of Shadowgate arrives. I really didn’t know what to anticipate until the game started. Unlike the previous game, this remake has three different modes with master being the most difficult. After choosing a difficulty mode, I was met with a familiar setting to the original classic. There was an air of nostalgia in the opening sequence, yet it was original and fresh - the design was fabulous. The background music was nicely adapted from the classic Shadowgate. A nice feature of the game is to switch the soundtracks to the original MIDI composition! A major difference at the start is you are met with a companion named Yorick, who not only guides you through your quest, but throws a few jokes and remarks to put you at ease in some frustrating situations. This was all before I entered the door - from here on I just knew this was going to be a master piece of a game. Boy was I right! The art work for the cut scenes later on were simply fantastic and suited well the nature of this point-and-click adventure game. The puzzles were similar to the classic though with more mind-boggling twist. They were that much better to solve. I couldn’t put the game down and even today, decades later, with the similarities from the previous game, the frustrations still arose. There are also a variety of side ‘missions’ for further achievements. With this in mind, this game is repayable, addicting and fun.
Zojoi takes the great problem solving of the original game to a whole new level.

Despite these negative reviews, I found the game appealing... just not in the same way the others were. I've played through the game, and finished the campaign without too much issue.
This game was finished, but not as I, or most would prefer to use the word. The developers succeeded in creating an incredibly amount of content and side missions, each with their own story and for the most part they aren't bugged. However, the quality of many parts of the game (especially the co-op) is severely lacking. I cannot even play the game with Uplay in online mode or else it crashes which I suspect is a bug grown from the Online- off the top of my head, I'd say it might be an issue with an anti-cheat system going awry. When I said this game was finished, I didn't say it was perfect or necessarily ready for release. I'm running on an AMD R9 270x without SLI or any of that, I have to comment that the quality is easily less than standard and some areas are strangely more buggy than others for reasons I can't quite describe (For example: regardless of the crowd size, I get between 19-25 frames per second, which keeps me near the number required for me to perceive true motion, but when I go to the cafe I drop down to 15-20).
The story was something else, it was far from overwhelming, it didn't make me feel like an assassin, and it certainly didn't live up to my expectations of an Assassin's Creed game. I'm sorry Ubisoft, but you just didn't pull off what I was expecting. Now, when I said it was something else that really should be thought about. It wasn't like the others and wasn't very incredible, but it wasn't bad. I knew what was happening and was able to follow my character's story well enough to get a grip of the situations and even felt sort of cool at times. My issue with the campaign is that it's short, ridiculously short. I'm following Arno Dorian across his search for vengeance, and there are times where I just don't know what's happening (but not as often as people emphasize), and times where it's really tugging at my heart chords but for god's sake Ubisoft, never make a game that short again! Ubisoft sacrificed their story in favor of multiplayer which honestly isn't something I'm thrilled about, seeing as I can't even use multiplayer until hopefully the next patch... maybe.
To finalize, the graphics were insane, they blew me away. The story was underwhelming, short, and♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off sometimes but it wasn't bad. There is a plethora of bugs that need to be addressed but nothing inherently game breaking. Game play itself is very fun (but you really need to get a hang of the controls before you start going where you want to and not jumping up every damn wall) and there is an insane amount of side-quests and other content to occupy your time, not just flags or feathers like some of the predecessors made the mistake of forcing us to collect. Multiplayer was incredibly fun, I loved it and can't wait to have it back because it was easily the best part of the game- even if I am somewhat mad at it overshadowing the story... a lot. Back to bugs, there are a lot regarding multiplayer, I've had to leave countless matches for getting stuck in between buildings (caught hanging under a roof that was merged with another building). Performance issues are no joke, they are debilitating but if you're not one to pay too much attention to them, then there's not much of an issue seeing as they rarely drop below 18 and tend to hover around the mid-20's on my rig (which is maybe a mid-level rig in terms of quality). I'd say it's a must buy, as a game alone it is incredible and really fun, with way more features than the other games... just a good number more bugs to accompany that. Buy it if you're a fan, but you probably shouldn't play it like a fan, or at least wait until the next patch comes out before making a big decision.
Thanks for your time!

Oh boy this game.
So I started playing a while ago after I saw many of my favorite streamers telling me good about it, the gameplay seemed fun etc.

I went into the game and loved it, the customization, mods, fun gameplay with hours and hours of stuff to do.

The attack animations are just the characters standing still with their weapons in an attacking stance, and it works. With some camera magic and more it looks ♥♥♥♥ing badass.

Afflictions basically make like terrible for you, stress your party, damage people, refuse heals etc. Virtues will buff your characters and remove stress. It's based on rng but certain things can change the chance.
That's all I need to say for now, buy this game.
And don't forget! "Overconfidense is a slow and insidious killer"

Jim's 10 words for 10 minutes review:

I want to like this game. I played a good chunk of it and it was fun. I want to like this game so much. I am incredibly upset that I have to recommend against buying it. I don't want to dislike it, and I suppose I don't; What I dislike is the idea that the game is dead in the water and looks like its going to be that way for... Well... Forever.
I got this game before it even came to steam. I bought the four pack straight from Chucklefish's main site. Played around in it, did all there was to do- I even have some hilarious screenshots of bugs that were fixed very early on. It was fun but eventually doing the same basic things over and over got very boring. The progression was basically broken past tier 2 (and there are 10 tiers) and if you wanted to make a nice base you had to luck out and find the right building materials on some planet. Which is fine, it was an alpha, I accepted it.
Fast forward to now. Almost nothing has changed. There is a little bit of tweaking here, some touch-ups there, but nowhere NEAR the amount of progress you'd expect from this amount of time. So I went back to their website and a wave of dread washed over me as I saw what I knew was the death knell of this game:
Several of the key developers advertising their personal pet project.
I heavily suspect they are using Starbound as a financial springboard for these projects. There is literally no other reason to do them besides ignorance. A studio as small as chucklefish can't AFFORD side projects like that, because all they do is take away from their primary project. Either they know this, and we're all being swindled so they can fund their pet projects (which, by the way, will likely be DOA, if not DNF, as most one-man projects turn out to be) or they do not realize this and they need to get their act together and put their personal projects on hold until Starbound is ready for release.
I am upset that I have to give this game a no-go. I wanted it to turn out good so much. The concept is here but the staff keeps side-tracking and delaying so they can work on petty dead-end distractions.

As you can see from my extremely high amount of hours played, My review will be a deal breaker for you.

I've been looking for a great hacking simulator like this for a very long time, but all I've found is overy dumbed-down, overly unrealistic, stupid games. I think that one great aspect of this game is the fact that it is terminal-based. Other hacking games I've seen just have a button that says "hack in". Once you press it, you're in, it's that simple, which makes it stupid. This game is actually pretty realistic hacking, the main difference being that you don't have to write the programs that you use to hack in. For example, if you were to tell your terminal to run a shell program, you would have to code a program called "shell" to download a ridiculous amount of cat videos off of the internet and send it to the proxy server. If you put the shell program in the bin folder with all of the built-in programs, if you just put "shell" in your terminal, it would work the same way that the game does. I also think that the storyline is great, with some random dialogue in people's computers to break the monotony.
-"You know what sucks?"
-"Vaccums."
-"You know what sucks in a metaphorical sense?"
-"Black Holes."
-"You know what just isn't cool?"
-"Lava?"
I laughed so hard that the sparkling water I was drinking at the time came straight out of my nose and on to my keyboard (thank god It's not broken, I paid $1200 dollars for this laptop).
Thank you for this fantastic game, it's the best I've played in a long time.

Its not easy being a cube and being a war cube is even worse, but you know what is the worst of all, that you are sent back to an old kingdom, Your Old Kingdom! By mister I am so funny narrator and everybody knows you and that you were the king. But given the fact that in this kingdom everyone is a cube and the fighting makes great fun and the fact that you are kind of a king, even if your mighty kingdom is run down by barbaric red cubes, it is not that bad.
That is kind of how the game of war cube starts, a small little combat game full of humor and all kind of medieval stuff. As already stated the game has good humor but I see the danger of this element becoming too powerful. In this state of the game the humor is hold back to an agreeable amount but if the game is going to define itself just through its humor, I may have to give it a bad review in the future.
The surrounding and different levels of the game are drawn beautifully in a now getting so popular low poly graphical style. The world (in this stage of the game) is rather small but given the fact that it is still in early accesses it is in place to hope that the scale of the game is getting bigger and bigger. Because now the game is finished in about 2 hours. Are this 2 hours fun? Yes they are but they leave the player with the slightly uncomfortable feeling of "I want more!" and "already finished?"
In the whole game there is no single indication of which weapon is the best and if the newly found armor is better than the other. A situation which let me to always fight with the same weapons what is not that bad (in this stage of the game) as the variety of armor and different weapons is almost equal to zero. Moreover I think a looting system where you can get some stuff out of the enemies you kill can help the game. I know it is not a revolutionary idea to make a looting system but I desperately want this game to be developed and to give the player more to do inside of the game because just exploring and good humor is not enough. Therefore I would also love to see a good development in the tactical view as I think the rather monotone getting combat system would match very well with a bit of strategic warfare with the tactical view. And moreover it would be interesting to see what bigger battles with warcubes would look like. As I said I think that is a huge area of development that would give the game great dimension. Because what the game does till now is creating a good framework. Now its time to get depth into the game and the different game assets.
I talked about a general framework of the game being created but this framework is also useful for something else, because this simple framework gives the player something to built his own imagination and own stories around. These aspect of the game principle is the same as in Mount and Blade  as the player can add to the game experience by his own imagination. For example when I hid in the bush and sneaked up to an enemy I was like "Whoa! That's a great experience I fell like I should have felt when I played Assassins Creed 3". No that is a bit over the top but I found it interesting that this simple game could generate the same feeling of excitement and anticipation as a huge game like AC 3.
In general the now existing early access game is rather small but is already playable and gives adequate game fun and I am especially excited how much potential this game has. So with more time put into development this game can become a real winner.

Don't.
The game looks pretty. It sounds pretty. The character development feels like it could be pretty.
The combat though... isn't good. It's slightly clunky but managable at first, but then you run into an enemy with a tower shield and the fun just jumps out the window and the tedium sets in.
It's a game that needs other options on how to deal with enemies, and pigeon-holes you into doing only one thing, regardless of what your spec happens to be. The fact that the rogue, for instance, needs FAITH to cast his spells (and be a rogue) should be a clue. The fact that a tank/warrior needs the same stat to cast HIS spells should also be a clue.
The classes don't really work the way they need to.
That's not even getting into how the combat feels, which is awkward.
Weapons and characters do not interact as if they are in the same world. I feel like the animation happens, then damage somehow happens. I don't feel like the weapon is connecting with anything. The weapons certainly don't connect with the terrain, which is a shame.
Weapon animations themsevles are largely dissapointing not just in visual appeal but also in practical use in combat. One of the first weapons you get is a greatsword from a boss, and it is arguably the best in damage for a strength based character but it is also almost useless due to it's slow animation speed and the fact that the move set is awkward in a fight.
Dodges are completely useless. They are too short, the invulnerablity is too short, and enemies will follow you through a dodge and hit you anyway if they are charging.
Sprinting is a pain in the butt on a controller. Holding down the same joystick you use to move is not a good idea for a sprint function. It's especially awkward since you need sprint to fight and you need sprint to JUMP. And jumping is required to get to certain areas.
Leveling up takes too long and the rewards for leveling up aren't that interesting.
Spells are limited and mostly boring at the start.
Some enemies (especially those with shields) are tedious to the point of frustration because their guard can't be easily broken, dodging around them doesn't work (they stick to you and rotate very fast), the kick attack is erratic and unreliable, and they don't seem to lose stamina when you hit the shield. They certainly don't lose more stamina than you do, and you stagger yourself if you hit a shield anyway.
The enemies animations always seem faster than yours, even when they are using a great weapon and you are using a 1h sword. For whatever reason, enemies always seem to interrupt your animation while it is very rare to interrupt theirs. This means you can be spammed to death by enemy attacks, while you cannot spam them to death. This is especially frustrating when dealing with multiple enemies at once. Gods help you if more than one of them has a shield, because using a strong sweeping attack certainly won't.
There are more things to complain about, but they all center around the combat system and controls. The thing is, 99% of the game is the fighting, and the fighting itself is tedious and frustrating. Unlike in Dark Souls where if you beat a monster that has been giving you issues and you feel elation, in this game I feel nothing. Ultimately, it feels like I didn't win. I feel like the game just randomly allowed me to win. Skill doesn't appear to play a part in how the game goes, which is exactly the opposite of what I wanted out of this game.
In short, don't buy it unless it is heavily discounted. I'm glad I waited and didn't get it at premium new release price ($50+) but I still feel that at $30 I could have spent my money elsewhere and been happier. The game looks really nice, but it doesn't play like a play-tested game. I feel like it was such a missed shot. They had everything they needed to give From a run for their money, but the one thing they didn't perfect bit them in the rear.

Qube is a short, but sweet 3D puzzle game (If you don't know the genre think of valve's portal)

Cons:
-Easy

Pros:
-Story
It was a great set up, till the end.
-Music
Amazing soundtrack fits the tone and situation well. nothing memoriable in my book, but still it's has an exceptional ost
-Atmostphere
It is both an awesome and cryptic place, you have no idea where you are, and where you are heading. This is the strongest comparison to portal.
-Variety

Qube is okay. I don't regret buying, or playing it. I'm just sad there was all lot of wasted potiental.

I am a veteran of the original Shadowgate which I played many years ago as a young boy on the Amiga 500. I was content at the fact Zojoi were reimaging the game with new hand drawn rooms and music, but to my surprise, what the developers have actually done is taken Shadowgate to a whole new level.
If you thought you knew how to conquer Shadowgate, think again. It is still the same nostalgic Shadowgate you once knew, with the same thematic puzzles, though now with a modern twist and level of complexity requiring a greater level of thinking and problem solving. Zojoi have also expanded Castle Shadowgate to introduce new areas of the game that were not accessbile or included in the original. The Steam achievement are also nice touch. Curing the curse in under 200 turns was a challanging achievement.
If you are not a thinker or problem solver then this game may not be for you. If you do get stuck (and you will) take a break to think about the puzzles. If you are still stuck the forum is very active and helpful, often providing you clues to solve the puzzles without actually providing you the spoiler.
Words cannot describe the feelings I get playing this. No modern game has kept me this entertained. At the price Zojoi are offering this, it is a steal!

I've seen my share of zombie movies and played my share of zombie games without ever becoming particularly impressed by any. Honestly I find most of them outright stupid, and with the zombie hype that has been going on the last few years the genre as a whole mostly leaves a foul taste in my mouth. But somehow I got talked into watching this show called "The Walking Dead" and it totally blew me over. Well written, great character building and feelings flying all over the board. I found it amazing that something related to zombies could be THAT good.
Then I learned about that this series, or rather the universe of that series, was going to be carried over to an episodic adventure type game by no other than Telltale Games. A company that has helped keeping the adventure genre of gaming alive when it felt almost extinct. As a BIG adventure game fan I have happily supported this company by getting mostly everything they have put out, and that was also mainly the reason I got this series as well.
I honestly had very little expectation of how this game series would be as I failed to see how it even would work to transfer the great writing and suspense that I experienced in the TV-series to an adventure type game. Even though I read good reviews of it I kept putting off playing it. I was absolutely certain that it was going to leave me disappointed.
Well, finally I got around to play it, and now I kick myself fo not playing it sooner. I can not believe how good this game is. I don't think I can remember better storywriting in any game I've played before. You really get to know the characters you meet and you get feelings and opinions about them. You're forced to make tough decisions in critical moments and you can never be sure if you did the right thing. Well, there is not really any clear right or wrong. There is mostly various shades of grey. Not only that, but your decisions affect the ones around you, and they will remember what you did or didn't do, and the game itself shapes itself around all this and creates different routes and takes on what you experience while playing through it.
All characters are masterfully voiced by a selection of excellent voice actors that helps making the experience close to magical. You'll find yourself laughing, crying, yelling at the screen and acting in panic. And you'll probably feel that you're in the middle of it all.
Now, it has to be said that this game is probably not for everybody. I can see, and even understand that people might find the gameplay itself to be a bit dull or repetetive and probably feel there is little gameplay at all. If you hate QTE's then you might want to shy away if you do not appreciate a good story. Also, even though I quite like the artstyle I see some people being thrown off a bit by the comic like cel shading, and I believe the game would be even better with a bit more realistic touch. It certainly looks good enough in its own way and should in any way be avoided with that as a reason.
I consider this game to be one of those games you absolutely should not allow yourself to miss out on. It is a game for the history books and you would want to tell your grandchildren that you were there to play it.
I rate this game 10/10
Recommended for everybody who appreciate video games, and their mothers too.

If you've never played a Half-Life game and aren't relatively familiar with the story and franchise, then this review might be for you. If you're just looking for a fresh perspective on one of your favorite classics then this review might also be for you. This was the first time I have ever played a Half-Life game. I'm afraid I missed it when it was released, however, I did play similar shooters from that era. I didn't think a review from me would be necessary for such a popular title like Half-Life but seeing that all of the top reviews for it are those ridiculous one or two sentence jokes, I thought that maybe my take on it would be welcome.
In Half-Life, you fill the shoes of Gordon Freeman, a theoretical physicist who's getting ready for an ordinary day at the office. Gordon Freeman apparently, dons his fancy HEV suit every morning after punching in on the time clock, and then runs around in a room that is not safe anyone not wearing said suit.
Long story short, something bad happens while on the job, and aliens decide to invade Gordon's workplace, Black Mesa labs. You then spend the rest of the game trying to get out of the now compromised Black Mesa facility. The structure is surprisingly large for a research lab and you'll spend quite some time traversing it's different levels, from labyrinthine industrial machinery to the sterile, clean laboratories where Freeman's colleagues go-a-sciencing. Without spoiling too much, the army becomes involved and for some unexplained reason, presumably a cover-up, considers you to be just as dangerous as the invading aliens.
That pretty much covers it, as far as an overall picture is concerned. You won't start with much, as far as weapons are concerned, however you'll slowly build up your collection as you romp through Black Mesa. The gameplay is smooth and uncluttered with too many bells and whistles. You run, shoot, and jump your way to the surface of the facility. Sometimes, you'll even push and pull some things to solve some very mild puzzles. The game can be quite challenging if you up the difficulty enough. And ammo is at a premium. You really have to think about what weapons you're using against which enemies and what is the most efficient way to kill them. Some weapons are better for killing different targets, which is a nice thing that makes this game more than just a mindless shooter.
There is little dialogue throughout this game. In fact, there are even a couple of levels where you won't encounter too terribly many enemies, however those are mostly reserved for the more industrial areas of Black Mesa.
The game is definitely dated, as it runs on the old 1998 GldSrc engine. If you're itching to get your nostalgia on, this can be a good thing, though. It reminded me a lot of Star Trek: Voyager - Elite Force from the early 2000's (unsurprisingly, as Raven Software admitted Half-Life was their inspiration for Elite Force). It can also be considered reminiscent of Doom, in it's tone, especially in the later levels I think. If you really just aren't in the mood of '98 graphics, thought, you could always get the Source version of the game, which isn't terribly different, but does give it that extra little oomph you may be looking for.
All in all, there weren't many cons in this game for me, except for it's lack of exposition. I think that may be more of a sign of it's age, however. Like I said, there isn't much dialogue and if you're looking for a lot of story, you won't really find it in this game. However, I've been told that HL2 has more of that sort of thing. I also mentioned above that ammo can be hard to find and many might consider that to be another negative trait. That's just something that will come down to personal preference, though. At least I never found myself bored while playing. The end boss was pretty unforgiving, though. The technical difficulty of defeating the final boss was fairly frustrating and they didn't exactly make the mechanics of doing it very smooth. This also seems to be a relic from gaming's past, though.
All things considered, I really enjoyed this game. I came it with mostly a fresh perspective, as I knew little about the tone of Half-Life and I knew little of the story. Even though I never played this as a kid, the nostalgia from shooters of it's era was enough to make me smile from time to time. If you played Quake III or games like it, you might also notice some of the minor similarities. When you consider that this was Valve's debut product, it makes it all seem that much more impressive.

Some gameplay:
Warcube is a little gem, it's pure fun from the ground up with a fantastic art style and neat controls. It is still early access because there is a fair amount still in contruction within the game world. You will often come across areas with traffic cones lining the environment and the developers own little cube character doing something amusing while he admits that he should be working on the game. It's great that the developer took the time to add these little characters and it really shows how much love he's poured into the game so far.
The controls are a simple affair, left and right mouse buttons control your main melee dash-attack and your ranged weapon respectively whilst you move around the world with WASD, space jumps. This allows the combat to remain fast but fluid, the slow motion combat kicking in when you chain attacks together. The combat can be challenging at times when arrows start raining down and the larger enemies forces you to keep changing your tactics.
The world that i've seen so far is well made and charming with many little characters to interact with. A great sense of humour is apparent in all these meetings which makes you want to explore and find new NPCs to talk to.
I would definately recommend this game, it's polished, charming and funny and at this price it's already a good deal. As more content is added, it may well evolve into a steal.

As with previous Xcoms, the stakes are high and the pressure is on and youll love every second of it.
Graphically the game does a great job of showing off particle effects and excellent lighting, and environments and character details look great. However gameplay is definitely where this game shines, as you constantly fight what feels like a superior force against what feels like a losing battle. You really do need to think tactically and use good strategies pull most of your soldiers out alive, but will frequently find that the overwhelming alien force is going to put someone in the hospital at almost any given battle.
Granted as you feverishly complete research and upgrades through careful resource management your troops will become more powerful and durable and you'll find them in the Infirmary at least for a shorter time. I did find with the right combination of soldiers and gear (not to mention some later upgrades) battles started to  become trivial. The thing is with the time and resource constraints and the constant pressure from the aliens, finding just the right combination of gear and soldiers is a challenge and then keeping them alive is in an even bigger one. (permadeath is a bitter sweet thing)
This game is not for someone looking for casual gameplay or an easy time, but more for people who are looking for a significant challenge and don't mind being under pressure at almost all times. There always felt like there was just one more thing I had to do, (research, resource gathering, battles, ect) before I quit so the game is definitely addicting.
Add to the fact that the game through the workshop is moddable, and you have even more (including the DLC), to enhance replayability.
I rate the game 9.5 out of 10 and give it a hearty recommendation for anyone looking for a visceral challenge with turn-based combat that has a wonderful sci-fi setting.

INTRODUCTION
At first, I thought this game would suck all the balls in the Chuck.E.Cheese ballpit. I mean, it mixes the graphics of Minecraft (Cause all the hip kids play it) and the gameplay of the modern FPS (cause all the hip kids play it). I ended up playing it, and it is only slightly flawed in a couple ways. So here it is, my review on Blockade 3D.
STORY
Like Turbo Dismount or Iron Snout, this game has no story whatsoever. Unless you consider 4 teams battling eachother because "Why the hell not" a story, there is no deep routes in the game explaining why they're all battling eachother. Personally, I don't care about having a story in a game like this, plus it's a Free To Play title afterall.
GAMEPLAY
I will say that gameplay is okay, just not great. The servers are a little difficult to connect to at times, probably because so many Russians play the game (I'm in North America, so I have to connect half way across the world to connect to some servers). And yes, Russians. The people that will beat the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of you in DOTA 2 or Call of Duty. So noobs will have a really hard time at first play session, but they can get used to things probably quicker than Smite (I've put like 50 hours into the game on my Xbox One, and I'm only starting to get the jist of things). There is a wide variety of modes, but the only fun ones are Infection (basically Halo's Flood mode) and Battle, which I've put the majority of time into. Otherwise, the other modes are boring or slow. Also, the game has a lot of weapons, but around 80 to 90 percent of the weapons are ones you have to pay for, so the game is Pay To Win.
PLAYERS
The player section is important to the review. Honestly, most players will wreck you hard. Like I said in gameplay, there's a lot of Russian players (Привет мой друг to you Russians). There can also be hackers, but their not that common. I've only met one once. He/She spawn killed everyone exept for the people on the hackers team. They won big time. I find it very rare to find another noob on another team. So you better get good at the FPS genre if you want to survive Blockade's players.
SUM UP: DO I RECCOMEND THE GAME?
I do reccomend this game if you are willing to pay money for skill (usually like 5 bucks, though) and you have a lot of time on your hands. The game isn't great enough for me to reccomend it to everybody, like how I reccomend Undertale & Just Cause 3 to everybody. It has a couple flaws, but besides that, I think it's an enjoyable game.
My Rating?
7.25/10

Absolutely love it. I'm just going to highlight some important things rather than going really in-depth
1. Progress. In every other f2p game, your progress is hampered by playing with bad vehicles when you first start out (ie lower tiers in WoT, WT, AW, ect). In this game, from the very moment you play your first game, every ship is balanced with each other. There are no tiers, so the only thing that determines victory is teamwork and skill, instead of time sunk in the game or money thrown.
The company made a genius system where ships at the bottom of the tree are the easiest to use, and ships at the top of the tree require more skill, but are still balanced.
2. Grind. One major major turn on for me is that you can play any ship from each of the three companies and it will help you progress up the tech tree. In short, you are not forced to play a ship that doesn't suit your playstyle to advance.
WoT is a major example of this cheap money grabbing method as you have to play intentionally crappy tanks like the amx40 to advance up the line. Not in fractured space, you can play anything you want within that company.
Grinding is reasonable. You won't be forced to play 1000+ battles to unlock a single top tier like in world of tanks. I played around 300 battles and unlocked around 75% of all available ships.
Crew. People complain that getting new crew members are expensive, but different crews only offer 1-2% differences in ship performance. Imo, they are mostly there to provide a personality to your ship.
3. Gameplay. Not a single ship works the same way as another. Everything is different with unique niches to fill in the battlefield, unlike WoT's t-54 and leopard 1 clones running around everywhere. You will feel your impact on the battle as your ship can do something that no other ship can do, rather at all or as well.
The game shifts from four different sectors with the majority of the battle taking place in alpha and beta lines. It is dynamic, and the design makes each engagement slow enough for tactical thinking but fast enough for it to be exciting.
There you have it. Give it a go and try this game out, everyone who was shafted by the f2p p2w games of the previous decade.
P.S. Real life money has no impact whatsoever for your ship's performance. There is no p2w content here and everyone is limited only by their skills and experience.
Skins -> only affects how your ships looks
Boosters -> you make more exp or credits, does not affect ship performance unlike gold shells
Crew-> like I said, the differences are only 1-2%. 1% increased speed means nothing in the overall battle

Thank you to Deck13 and CI games for development and publishing Lords of The Fallen. I enjoyed the world and charcters you provided for me to escape.
As i end my run of LOTF during new game + and reflect my on experience it reminds me of a successful turn-based game(Aarklash Legacy) that stripped away a lot of "trending" RPG systems to the bone while focusing more on gameplay. I think thats exactly what LOTF also has done though with mixed results but it has more me excited for a sequel rather than another Dark Souls.
LOTF is a 3rd person action game in which you play as Harken(no charcter custimization) a criminal that has been sprung from jail from a mysterious monk named Kaslo. Kaslo insist you are the one to defeat the evil rhogar and the revived God Adyr as it takes evil to slay evil. Though Harken wears his crimes on his face with markings(very cool)it is only mentioned briefly from a run in with a guard and we never know what crimes he committed. A big opportunity missed in that regard. Along this story quest you will face a few decisions that will decide one of three possible endings. Its a good video game story with good voice acting but none of it was memorable. Its all pretty standard by now, but more effort is here than expected and its actually a story rather than pieces and speculation.
Once you start the game you are only given 3 classes to choose the cleric, warrior, and rouge which for story reasons makes sense. All charcters have pre made stats so custimization is minimal. I chose the rouge class which from my understanding is considered hard mode and at the start it is very diffcult as a slight breeze seemed to kill me. Fortunantley you are able to level quickly but it took a good 10 hrs before i felt powerful. Leveling your character is pretty normal as you slay enemies and complete quests you are rewarded with XP which you will distribute through either upgrading your magic(4 spells x 3 upgrades) or physical (6 options STR/VIT/END/FAITH/AGI/LUCK). Again comapared to a lot of RPGs these upgrades while minimal i think actually made it easier to maintain the specific charcter you envisioned at the start.
Gaining experience does come with its caveat of risk and reward. In LOTF the longer you stay alive and kill enemies a multiplier for XP will continue to increase(x2.0 max) and If you die your 'ghost' will be waiting for you to return. However, your ghost will dissolve based on the stregnth of the multiplier. The larger the multiplier the longer it will be visible and at 100%. I like this idea but it is basically null becasue of checkpoints are located everywhere. I can only think of one instance where i was not able to retrieve my ghost and it was just a dumb mistake on my part.
LOTF also does not follow todays trend with a massive open world but a more confined semi linear castle exploration design. This made for walking around slow and steady and some of the levels are good but late near the end game i was totally lost and could not recall where to go. Dont be mistaken there are some levels that are outdoors but for the most part action is in tight hallways. The level and quest design also plays into LOTF no hand holding policiy which i love but if you want to make it easier on your self keep notepad and pen close.
Not suprising as with any title today i recall LOTF did have some launch issues with some bugs and graphical glitches but other than a crash or 2 the game played and looks amazing. The envorments, weapons, enemies and charcters all have a heavy metal vibe and the sound design maybe some of the best for this type of genre i have heard. The thud of weapons against shields, echoes in the caverns and just the wind blowing all make for a very immersive experience.
As a rouge i moved fast and with the spells available i was pretty powerful late in game but getting in close against enemies was high risk. However a majority of fighting is always one on one so encounters are not too difficult. I pretty much used either daggars or these awesome wolverine like claws  as weapons and late in the game i found out somthing i did not know. Without spoilers it basically changed everything about my charcter and i suddenly became a real bad♥♥♥♥♥  If LOTF has its 'thing' its these hidden secrets about weapons, bosses and quests. After i completed the game and found out some of the secrets i was suprised how deep and how many there actually are becasue in In game you would never know.
After my initial playthrough i started up new game + which a rarely do but becasue i wanted to see if any higher gear would drop and i was really dissapointed. Enemies and loot did not scale and i basically walked through the first 4 bosses without a scartch. If it did scale who knows i proabably would still be playing.
LOTF is a good new action RPG that compliments other titles in the genre but seperating itself in some new and exciting ways.  It doesnt follow todays RPG trends of needing a huge open world, 100hr campaign, and deep crafting system it relys on good ol' game and gameplay and that is always welcome in my librbary.
Positives
A solid 3rd person action RPG game that doesnt take 100 hrs to complete
Enviroments, weapons, charcters and enemies look great
Sound design is incredible
Nice clean UI
No hand holding
Level design is ok, but i would like to have seen the world more interconnected
Some bosses are great
A lot of 'hidden' content for quests, bosses and equip
You can break the game making it easy
Negatives
Too many Checkpoints decrease the tension, maybe an option to decrease for difficulty?
Enemy variety
Some bosses were very basic in design pattern
No scaling for enemeis or loot in new game +
the balance of enemies and spells  fells off- you are OP
Not a lot of difference in spells from each type of charcter choice
Crafting is quite shallow
Inventory UI could be better-cant drop items
Notes:
I played on my desktop PC with an R9 390 video card
I have about 30+ hrs in one full playthough and upto the 4th boss on new game +
I played the game at 1080P/ 60 running smooth with 1-2 crashes
I used an Xbox controller

QUBE has a nice aesthetic, and uses simple, easy to understand pieces to build complex and often devious puzzles. When things click for you, it feels great. However, some bits in the game left me frustrated, rather than interested, and I admit I turned to a guide once or twice in the later stages just to advance. (Of course, that may be a reflection on my abilites rather than the game's difficulty or quality of level design.) The narrative was interesting enough and well presented, but somehow lacking at the end. There are a couple of secret areas you can go back to, and the Director's Cut includes some DLC with time trials and the like if the gameplay continues to interest you after completing the story.
Being a first-person physics puzzle game with a glossy, stark art style, it's hard not to compare Q.U.B.E to Portal; if you enjoyed those types of puzzles, you will find things to like in this game, but without Valve's level of polish. Despite recommending it, I felt as much relief as accomplishment when I finished; it was entertaining, but I was ready to move on.

After completeing the game in only 15 hours, it appears obvious just how much of a rush job this game really was. Poor quality through out the entire game. Lack of enemy variety, clunky combat system and awful sound effects make this game a real bore to play. I pretty much forced myself to playthrough this just to see where it would lead.
I have nothing positive to say about this game, it has no redeeming values. Even if you buy this for $5 you aren't going to have a good time. Not even an okay time. This isn't just mediocre, it's poorly executed and riddled with bad design.
I can't say I experienced any moment of fun. Everything this game tries to do, other games have done better. You might think "well it looks pretty good at least" it really doesn't. To get this game to run at around 45 fps i had to turn off EVERY graphical option and set textures to Medium at 720p. It runs horribly on a brand new gaming PC that runs other current gen games at 60+ fps on 1080p. So needless to say, it looked pretty bad for me.
Sound effects are terrible as well. There's about 3 weapon sounds in the game and you will hear them a million times. They don't sound powerful or realistic at all. Many missing sounds for a lot of enemies and environmental things. Cutscenes often feel like they are lacking sounds or the sounds are too quiet or just don't match what you are seeing.
I turned the music off because I thought it was pretty awful too. Some of the boss music sounds like a parody of symphonic music and doesn't feel intense at all. The tracks that aren't completely awful are generic at best.
It's not a very difficult game either and that's coming from someone who created the worst build possible. I put all my points into HP, MP, stamina and equip load. (I did this because I was under the impression that there would be plenty of faith-scaling weapons since i had one very early in the game) This meant that I couldn't use 90% of the weapons and shields. While I had good defense, probably too much considering I barely took damage in the later half of the game, I couldn't use any weapons or block effectively. I two-handed a weak staff for the first half of the game which took forever to kill anything. Than I finally got a good faith-scaling weapon, grinded super easily and eventually found a super low strength requiring sword that dealt way more damage than the 3 faith weapons i found in the entire game. So i used that for the end game areas.
With that, you can get an idea of how poorly balanced the game is. Later weapons in the game completely replace early game weapons as the scaling is completely useless for most weapons. There is no upgrade system either, just a rune slot system for weapons, shields and armor and only the higher strength and agility weapons have slots so none of the weapons i used through out my playthrough had any slots. a completely useless system that i never even got to experience outside of giving my armor extra defense.
Bosses are so bad in both design and gameplay. Some are completely broken such as getting stuck in walls or in one case I had a boss completely stand still the whole time as I slowly chipped away at his massive health pool. Most of the bosses have a ton of health so it can take ages to kill them but luckily they are very slow and predictable doing the same moves over and over again. Rolling is mostly useless in this game so you can't roll through most boss attacks so it's a waiting game, you just have to wait for that split second after they perform a combo to get a hit or two in, back away and repeat. This "technique" will work on every boss in the game even though it is extremely tedious and with the final boss, there's barely any oppertunities to safely get a hit in. Most of the bosses will ALWAYS knock you down when they hit you, even with heavy armor and really high poise. Ground pounds are very common and will knock you down from a good 15 feet away from the boss.
Another example of poor quality is the overabundance of glitches and bugs. It almost seems like nothing really works as fully intended. Hitboxes can be really messed up, getting hit from attacks that don't make physical contact with you or in some luckier cases, boss attacks going right through you but you recieve no damage. If you are casting a spell (which you only get 4 in the whole game) and you get hit towards the end of the long animation, you will recieve the effect of the spell but lose no MP. This made healing during boss fights really easy so I didn't have to rely on potions too much. Slidy collision detection makes walking on stairs really weird. The lock on system is bogus, barely functional. You have about a 10% chance of being able to change target when locked on. Sometimes the camera won't even face the enemy you are locked on to but you still walk toward the enemy, this killed me in quite a few areas involving pitfalls.
Level design. It's there and it involves lots of switches, back tracking and locked doors. Early areas aren't so bad, they seem pretty average at first but then you get to the middle of the game and it just gets worse from there. Narrow cooridors, enemy ambushes, floating blocks and jumping across gaps as well as pitfalls galore. Many times I had to look up a guide to find out where to go because progressing through the later game is so convoluted. You need to pull several levers to open one door sometimes, or to move some blocks around to progress. This isn't exactly obvious when you will see a switch next to a gate and expect that switch to do something. You pull the lever, nothing happens. What?!
Despite all these problems, I still didn't die too much. Most of the time it felt pretty cheap when I did die. Enemies like the mages can drain your HP really quickly, shoot really fast magic that deals huge damage and knocks you down, cast a buff that drains your stamina and every time you hit them, it deals equal damage to you, these guys can end you very quickly. There are checkpoint crystals in rooms with 3 enemies sometimes so as soon as you die and respawn you are getting attacked. Getting cornered by 2 enemies with greatshields and repeatedly attacks results in no posibilities of survival. Speaking of greatshields, you can't kick through them, attack through them or do ANYTHING to counter them. If you do stagger them, you won't even have enough time to get a SINGLE hit in with how slow these weapons are. Only way I could kill them is with magic which seem to go right through their shields making them easy. Otherwise you would be screwed.
The story, ha. It's run of the mill and has poor voice acting and writing. Some of the worst stuff I've seen. Awkward animations that keep repeating when npc's are talking combined with non-existent personalities makes none of the characters appealing or relatable. Even after seeing the ending of this game, I didn't have a clue what I had really done in the game plotwise. I don't even know who the final boss was, just kinda there. I assume it was a certain character but it's never explained why there's a big demon beastie as the final boss. Also plotholes as you can expect. How do the [end game enemies] know I supposedly betrayed them? Nothing here really makes much sense and the world is so generic and boring you won't really care.
I think that just about covers everything. The TL;DR version is: don't buy the game. It's garbage. No, really. Don't even think about it. I don't care if it's on sale, it's bad. Really bad, probably much worse than you can imagine. You like Dark Souls? That's cool and all but this is nothing like it. Not even a low budget version of it, it's more like if you had taken Dark Souls and shattered it on the ground and tried to reassemble it but you have several large chunks missing and it just looks hideous. That's Lords of the Fallen.

Alright, alright, alright. I keep seeing bad reviews for this game because people think that it's no longer updating. That's not right. Starbound creators have been holding off on lots of small updates in lue of one big update, that will make the game feel much more full of content and context. They've recently said that the large update will be out before the end of the year. Sidenote: If you'd like to follow the updates so far, and their day to day progress and what exactly they're updating and progressing on, just go to their website.

So yeah, outside of just putting this info out there, I'd like to say that this is easily one of my favorite games. It's wonderful in terms of replayability, graphics and just general gameplay. The story part isn't too large right now, but that's being massively extended upon. The two best qualities about Starbound as of right now, though, are the Explore and Create traits. You can explore planet after planet, solar system after solar system, and universe after universe. You can also use all blocks in game to design and build endlessly everywhere you go. This is essencially the same gameplay trait that so many people love about Minecraft, yet in a 2D form, more related to that of Terraria.
In general, this game is great. It's fun, beautiful, and it IS going to be updated. I know that it's hard to keep waiting, but it's coming. Don't lose heart in it yet. Chucklefish will come through. (Remember they're a company with other games they're working on too. They haven't give up on Starbound. Just give it time.)

Yes it is hard, yes it is brutally punishing, yes it is a lot of RNG that can go against you, but that is how it is supposed to be and what makes it fun. The combat is turn based strategy, but it takes a lot of strategy aside from combat to succeed, e.g. you need to choose the right team compositions and trinkets for the mission you want to do.
With time and experience (skills,trinkets,provisions,compositions,etc.) you'll be able to tweak a lot of the probabilities involved to your favor. BUT you can be perfectly prepared and still party wipe on any trash mob. This may upset you because you invested a lot of effort into those characters, but in the end you did not lose a lot. You can just take 4 new heroes, do 5 dungeons with them and you'll be in the same position as before. Just consider every character in your estate as expandable.
Nothing in this game needs a nerf, you can beat everything with preparation, patience and maybe a more than one try.

Too Far, Too Fast, and In What Direction?
Hype is a terrible thing. Especially when it’s directed by Ubisoft’s incredible marketing team. Seriously, they should be showered with praise for their ability to spin the titles of the Assassin’s Creed franchise into something that their “consumer base” will want to consume.
For everyone thinking that this was just a continuation of Ubisoft’s money spinning of this franchise, you’re simply looking for a simple excuse for, let’s face it, a game that didn’t make par because the developer threw the hype train into high gear on the day of reveal. That’s not to say that I’m disagreeing with you.
Yes, the game is riddled with bugs. Yes, the software runs like a sloth on hallucinogens. Yes, the service supposedly handling the load of multiplayer isn’t doing its job.
But people are forgetting that a tonne of people at Ubisoft put their heart and soul into making this game BE the next-gen title that we and they were hoping for. The artists, especially; the texture, level and environment designers; the guys behind mo-cap, animation and voice capture; hell, even the actors behind the mo-cap did a decent job.
The people that should be getting an earful are, firstly, the optimisation team. Either that or they should be getting bereavement for being harassed because they had a deadline out of their control. Secondly, the people that are in charge of the online services, connectivity and servers; OR those in charge who FORCED the game out with the online services not being fully ready.
30% of the issues with the game would be and hopefully WILL BE sorted with connectivity fixes, another 30% with the fixes to game optimization.
The last 40% are simply arguable issues with the game itself. It seems like Ubisoft pushed too far too fast, wanting to claim this dream of a “next-gen” gaming experience. The combat feels organic, but is too interrupted by sometimes irritating camera angles and a lack of warning when you’re about to be shot-fodda, or smacked in the head with an axe. The immersive Paris with randomly generated side-events is nice, but far too samey to be enjoyable for the length of a full play through, especially considering the size of the city. The open-ended assassinations would be a nice change, if you weren’t funnelled down a predictable path determined by “optional” opportunities that help you get the mission done.
The Helix interludes are nice little morsels of distraction from the main game. But even they are let down by again, being too samey, and secondly, reminding all the fans of the series that there is a world OUTSIDE the simulation that seemingly, plays little to no part in what happens INSIDE it.
All in all- the game deserves a 7.5/10. Maybe an 8. But as it stands, until these fixes get fixed, it can only stand at a 5.
Get it. Give the massive team that worked on this the recognition they deserve. But only do it if things get fixed (stay posted), and or when the game drops in price. Just don't be an♥♥♥♥♥and post a mindless negative review because you're too selfish to see the work that actually went into the game.

Darkest Dungeon is one of the better new games I've played in awhile, and it's scratching an itch that I've had for a long time.
The game is difficult, punishing, and from start to finish is a tense experience. When playing, I'm constantly either fearing for the lives of the characters I put so much work into developing, or worried about what to invest my previous money or resources into, or how to properly deal with the stress and quirks that build up after going into the dungeons.
The game is not for the faint of heart for sure, if you're not a fan of challenging games, or don't enjoy dealing with the negative consequences of failure, this is definitely not the game for you. This is a game for people who want to constantly be at edge, biting their nails at the worst of times and feeling sweet relief wash over them at the best of times.
It also has an amazing art style, one of the best I've seen in ages, and as a result I can see this game aging like a fine wine in the long term.

I just couldn't stop playing this game. If you're familiar with Linux prompt commands, this will be an easier game for you. However, it will still be enjoyable for the lore, the humour, and exploring folders and files outside the main story.
This is mainly a text based game, but the UI is well laid out.  You can do most of the accessing through text commands but clicking through folder hierarchies to access files is also possible and quicker (speed is a factor at times).
The story is rich and well written enough to want to know more about the characters involved. This makes the contracts seem more fleshed out instead of just doing hacker jobs for the sake of it like in Uplink, which I assume is the inspiration for this game. And some contracts are challenging enough to keep things interesting gameplay wise; akin to Portal where when you figure out a puzzle you feel clever for the accomplishment.
I'm really picky with games and rarely play through them completely, but Hacknet had me hooked from start to finish. I highly recommend it.

(X turns to eliminate this guy)
etc. etc.
Now along with the the timer being really annoying the lack of mission variety is also upsetting but it didn't bother me THAT much.
The amount of new enemies is also a little lacking. Yeah you're fighting Advent which is mostly made of humanoid aliens with normal guns and robots but this is XCOM, a game about fighting aliens and the aliens aren't even fought that often.
I mean don't get me wrong XCOM 2 introduces 13 new enemies in the base game as opposed to Enemy Unknown's 11. This means XCOM 2 has a total of 18 enemy types and that sounds all fine and dandy until you realize that at least 7 of those are Advent enemy types and only 6 of those are brand new aliens. That means only 5 enemies from EU came back for XCOM 2. The new aliens are kind of cool to fight but for the most part you're fighting Advent forces which means you'll be fighting Soldier after Officer after Lancer after Mech after Heavy Mechs after Turrets after Shieldbearer and so on...
However the positives do outscale the negatives by a lot.
The story and the concept of a resistance movement fighting an evil leadership is nothing new but there is something unique about XCOM 2 that makes it fresh and exciting.
You might be thinking well why is there a sequel if I beat the first game? Well if you beat the game and got every achievement... I have some bad news.
In Enemy Unknown you were a super beefed up organization funded by the governments of the world and now you find out you lost
and have to rejoin the fight with little to no equipment
This is definitely the best part about XCOM 2 and the gameplay revolves around you being the underdog. In Enemy Unknown you were the one hunting the aliens and in this game it's vice versa. THEY are the hunter and YOU are the prey. You can't go guns blazing and expect to not lose someone (this is XCOM after all). The Concealed mechanic is amazing for getting the drop on the enemy and really sets up some killer ambushes. In addition you actually have to scavenge for supplies and get items from enemy drops or fly the Avenger to a scavenging site. The black market in this game actually makes a little more sense because of the scenario you're put in.
Overall I would highly recommend this game. It is much harder than Enemy Unknown and I can guarantee you that you will lose some of your best men, but hey that's what having lots and lots and
of saves are for.
Good luck out there Commander.

Much better than the first game, but still not up to my expectations when Mundi's name is on it.  While there are a few good HOGs in this title, they are few and far between.  Most of them are single-item hunts (e.g. find only feathers) which are far less enjoyable than the "find random crap on the screen" style puzzles, but admittedly that's just personal preference, and those ones do make an appearance albeit sparsely.
The story is nonsense, but I don't really think anyone plays these games for the story.  Suffice to say that doesn't have the standard "horror" element to it, so those who are typically put off by Mundi's cheap startle-scare thrills (always fun) will have nothing to worry about here.  Still, there's some stuff here that might give some kids nightmares (a little off-screen violence and the overall dark tone of the story) and some that might give adults nightmares (Mundi tradition of creepy animated children who talk funny).
On the plus side, it's a solid romp and none too difficult on expert difficulty, though you may find yourself stuck at times (protip: there's probably a HOG that has appeared on a previous room).  The extra hidden sigil quest is pretty easy this time around as you are notified when one is in the room you're in.  Also, there's no need to contend with mind-numbing alternatives to the HOGs (like mahjong when you suck at finding stuff) and therefore no need to play through the game again just to get them achievements.  Unfortunately, for those who -do- enjoy those minigames instead of solving the HOGs, you're out of luck here.

>Lighter, more agile vessels can exploit these - it keeps the fight dynamic and tactical!
+Choose your target - hammering the rear-side of an enemy ship does much higher levels of damage.
>Flanking tactics are an excellent way of gaining the advantage.
-Higher tier ships can be a grind to aquire - though it's not too exausting.
-Very few players at the moment, often you may bump into the same players in games.
>The game needs you!! Join us!
EDIT: When I say "higher tier" I do not intend to suggest that some ships are better than others; higher tier ships are more specialised or just more bulky.
Such ships include 'sniper'-like vessels, and/or stealth cruisers. VERY large ships, such as the Gladiator are certainly late in the unlock tree, and going against one in a starter ship solo is considered suicide - yes - but this does not make it a 'better ship'. The Gladiator for instance sacrifices movement speed for it's extremely tanky armour and damaging armaments. You can easliy out-fox the thing if it finds itself agressively pushing; just sneak past and cap their base, it won't be able to catch you!
Like I said earlier - play smart. Know the weaknesses and strengths of the ships you use and fight against, and you'll have fun. :END EDIT

Well first off, it's 2017 and I'm finally playing CoD games again. Some I missed as I was working 70 hour weeks for 10 years straight it seemed and some I sort of remember. Ok, now getting past that I can give you my outtake on this game. I actually played the newer CoD's and went from new graphics to old. This doesn't bother me at all. I see people loving 8 pixel games, but this looks like crap to them. If you do some research you will notice that 3D just came out for the PC around the release of this game (CoD 1 and this Add-On). The graphics are great for what they had to work with. Audio was great, Music has that good ol' war feel during the victory scenes, etc. Voice dubbing was ok as these guys didn't have the budget to hire Keefer yet (reference to World at War). I'll take the silly voices over wasting 1 million on Keefer. Not sure if it was before 24 but yeah, it gave this game a TON more fun.
Coming from playing CoD 1, that game seemed to never end (in a good way). I was coming home and spending hours on regular mode and just keep going and going. The missions were all different so it wasn't redundant or anything just you got more money worth of mission time. Personally, I think this "add-on" is better then the CoD 1. This one has you up in the plane shooting down planes, fun tank missions, and some things the first didn't. So it's not some money grab, it is different.
If you know history well, they really put some good stuff in here. Going through all the countries and playing as the US, British, and working with allies was great. You don't get the military channel videos on this if I can recall (I'm somewhat mixed up on the cut scenes from part 1 and this) but they have some nice history letters and some animations with the 3D models and all.
Gameplay seems better on this then the first to me. It seems like you were hitting people where you pointed better. So they did add some fixes to it as things were evolving and went into CoD 2. Playing on regular (default difficulty) was a good challenge for me. I am a keyboard and mouse guy. I can't play the joystick on these games. I love the joystick for Rocket League and those games, but not these 1st or 3rd person games. The movement was good for such an old game it works flawless on my Nvidia 970. I maxed it out of course and I remember back when this came out I couldn't do to it as is required a better video card and I was younger. Mommy wouldn't buy it! Lol. So yeah, it was a smooth journey for sure.
